metadata.executor_model: opus (fresh-context general-purpose subagents), the session default
metadata.release_gate_for: P14c v0.51.0 — a contract defect escalates instead of dead-ending
metadata.baseline_note: without_skill baseline intentionally skipped: regression detection plus one new eval.

notes: FOUR paths, four behaviours, and the stub appears in exactly one. That separation is what this release buys and it cannot be verified without running all four: happy path persists/matures/commits (no stub); invalid input is a Guardrails rejection (no stub); unreachable store is a blocker (no stub); a self-contradicting contract is a blocker WITH a stub.

Eval 3 is in this gate although the release is not about it: T2 split the single sentence that routed ordinary rejections, and a split that leaked them into the new branch would turn rejections into blocked runs. It did not. Its executor reasoned it in the release's own terms without being prompted: 'the contract is coherent; this input just cannot satisfy it'.
Eval 5 was seen red before T2 existed: the run blocked correctly and had nowhere to put its evidence (2 FAIL on the escalation assertions, 4 PASS on the refusals).

The stub the green run wrote quotes both conflicting clauses verbatim and derives the real range from Rule 2, proving the conflict is structural rather than particular to the input. A and O left open; status line 'blocked, nothing applied'.

Every executor was given an explicit no-external-state constraint this time, and none published to an artifact URL. The two earlier deviations (v0.49.0, and this slice's red run) were a missing instruction, not model caprice — worth knowing before treating such a deviation as a model problem.

OBSERVED IN ALL FOUR RUNS, and in every run this session: no host task system was available, so step 0's 'materialize each contract Rule as a visible task' never happened and the JSONL ledger served as the only task surface. The skill prescribes a surface that has not once existed in practice. Not a defect of this release; recorded because eight-for-eight is evidence, not noise.

Eval 3's executor reported a second real gap it deliberately did not act on (the skill caps maturation at one refinement per run): the contract's frontmatter `metric` covers only the success path, so a run ending in rejection has nothing declared to verify itself against.
Counts are the grader's own PASS:/FAIL: lines.
